 class CM-BGP

control-plane
 service-policy input PM-COPP

ccna_vlan_trunk_native_hardening.title: CCNA Guided Build: VLAN Trunk Native VLAN Hardening
ccna_vlan_trunk_native_hardening.symptom: Build and verify secure trunk behavior across distribution and access switches from requirements.
requirements: Create VLAN 10 (USERS_A), VLAN 20 (USERS_B), and VLAN 999 (NATIVE_BLACKHOLE) on DIST1, DIST2, ACC1, and ACC2.
Configure DIST1<->ACC1 and DIST2<->ACC2 links as 802.1Q trunks.
Set native VLAN to 999 on all configured trunk links.
Restrict allowed VLAN list on trunks to 10,20,999.
Ensure access ports for hosts use VLAN 10 or VLAN 20 as labeled in the topology notes.
Verify trunk state, native VLAN, and allowed VLAN consistency end-to-end.

faults.fault: Starter baseline omits hardened trunk settings and native VLAN controls.
faults.fix: Implement all listed requirements and verify output alignment.

hints: Create VLANs first on all participating switches, then apply trunk settings.
Use one interface as a golden template and replicate on peer trunk ports.
Validate both native VLAN and allowed VLAN list in show interfaces trunk output.
expected_results: All required VLANs exist on each participating switch.
Target links are trunking with native VLAN 999.
Allowed VLAN list is limited to 10,20,999 on each trunk.
Endpoint-facing access ports map to intended VLANs.

answer_key.root_cause: Lab is configuration-first; secure trunk and VLAN baseline must be built from requirements.
answer_key.fix_summary: Create VLANs and apply hardened trunk settings (native VLAN 999 and allowed VLAN restrictions) on required links.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch A initial guided build lab.
progression_rank: CCNA Guided Build: VLAN Trunk Native VLAN Hardening
walkthrough_steps: Identify trunk-facing interfaces between distribution and access layers from topology labels.
Create VLANs 10, 20, and 999 on all required switches.
Configure trunk mode and 802.1Q encapsulation where required by platform.
Set native VLAN 999 on each trunk link.
Restrict allowed VLAN list to 10,20,999 on each trunk.
Assign endpoint access ports to VLAN 10 or 20 per host intent.
Run verification commands and capture output proving native/allowed VLAN consistency.
coaching_notes: Mismatch native VLANs are a common issue; always verify both ends of each trunk.
Avoid allowing all VLANs by default; explicitly constrain the trunk VLAN list.
Access-port misassignment often appears as one-way reachability; verify switchport mode and access VLAN.

ccna_router_on_a_stick_intervlan.title: CCNA Guided Build: Router-on-a-Stick Inter-VLAN Routing
ccna_router_on_a_stick_intervlan.symptom: Implement inter-VLAN routing using a single router trunk link and verify end-to-end reachability.
requirements: Create VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 on the access/distribution path used for the lab.
Configure the switch uplink toward router as an 802.1Q trunk carrying VLANs 10 and 20.
Create router subinterfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 with dot1Q encapsulation.
Assign default-gateway addresses to each VLAN on the router subinterfaces.
Assign host-facing access ports to the correct VLANs.
Verify cross-VLAN connectivity and routing-table entries.

faults.fault: Starter baseline lacks router subinterfaces and trunk mapping.
faults.fix: Build subinterfaces, trunk, and VLAN assignments per requirements.

hints: Configure switch VLANs and trunk first, then router subinterfaces.
Encapsulation VLAN IDs on subinterfaces must match switch VLAN IDs.
Use brief show commands after each step to catch typo-driven failures early.
expected_results: Hosts in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 reach their respective gateway IPs.
Inter-VLAN ping succeeds through router subinterfaces.
Router shows connected routes for both VLAN subnets.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab: inter-VLAN services are intentionally absent in baseline.
answer_key.fix_summary: Configure trunk + router subinterfaces with matching VLAN IDs and gateway addressing.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch A guided build lab.
progression_rank: CCNA Guided Build: Router-on-a-Stick Inter-VLAN Routing
walkthrough_steps: Identify router-facing switch uplink interface.
Create VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 on involved switch(es).
Set uplink as trunk and allow VLANs 10,20.
Create router subinterface for VLAN 10 with encapsulation dot1Q 10 and gateway IP.
Create router subinterface for VLAN 20 with encapsulation dot1Q 20 and gateway IP.
Place host ports into correct access VLANs.
Run verification and confirm cross-VLAN reachability.
coaching_notes: Most failures are VLAN ID mismatch between trunk and subinterface encapsulation.
For subinterfaces, parent physical interface must be up/no shut.

ccna_ospf_single_area_baseline.title: CCNA Guided Build: OSPF Single-Area Baseline
ccna_ospf_single_area_baseline.symptom: Build a clean single-area OSPF baseline and verify adjacency and route exchange.
requirements: Enable OSPF process 10 on core/distribution routers used in the path.
Set explicit router IDs per device.
Advertise all inter-router transit links in area 0.
Advertise loopback or LAN test prefixes in area 0.
Set passive interfaces for non-neighbor-facing ports where appropriate.
Verify full adjacency and learned OSPF routes on each router.

faults.fault: OSPF process and network statements are intentionally incomplete in baseline.
faults.fix: Implement complete single-area OSPF requirements across participating routers.

hints: Bring up interfaces and IP addressing first before enabling OSPF.
Use passive-interface default plus selective no passive-interface on peering links.
Confirm area values are consistent on both sides of each adjacency.
expected_results: All intended adjacencies reach FULL state.
Each router learns remote OSPF routes.
OSPF interface brief output matches design intent.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab: OSPF control plane is intentionally not fully configured.
answer_key.fix_summary: Configure OSPF process/router-id/networks/passive policy for a complete area 0 baseline.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch A guided build lab.
progression_rank: CCNA Guided Build: OSPF Single-Area Baseline
walkthrough_steps: Confirm addressing on all inter-router links.
Enable OSPF process 10 and set router ID on each participating router.
Advertise transit networks into area 0.
Advertise loopback/LAN networks into area 0.
Apply passive-interface policy with exceptions for peering links.
Verify FULL neighbors and OSPF routes.
Document discrepancies and remediate until outputs match expected state.
coaching_notes: Area mismatches and wildcard typos are the two most common misses.
Neighbor comes up only when both routing and L3 interface state are correct.

senk_asav_inside_outside_nat.title: SENK Guided Build: ASAv Inside-Outside Dynamic NAT Baseline
senk_asav_inside_outside_nat.symptom: Implement baseline inside-to-outside NAT on ASAv and verify translation and policy behavior.
requirements: Configure inside and outside interface security levels and addressing as defined in lab brief.
Define object network for inside subnet.
Configure dynamic PAT from inside subnet to outside interface.
Allow ICMP/required test traffic from inside toward outside test target.
Verify xlate and conn tables during traffic tests.
Ensure return traffic is handled as expected by stateful inspection.

faults.fault: NAT and related policy are intentionally incomplete in starter baseline.
faults.fix: Build object NAT/PAT and permit policy required for inside-to-outside access.

hints: Validate interface roles (inside/outside) before NAT configuration.
Confirm object network subnet mask accuracy; /24 vs /25 mistakes are common.
Generate traffic before checking xlate/conn tables.
expected_results: Inside hosts can reach outside test destination per policy.
xlate table shows dynamic translation entries.
packet-tracer confirms expected permit path for test flow.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab: inside/outside NAT policy is intentionally absent in baseline.
answer_key.fix_summary: Define inside object, apply dynamic PAT to outside interface, and verify with traffic + xlate/conn checks.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch A guided build lab.
progression_rank: SENK Guided Build: ASAv Inside-Outside Dynamic NAT Baseline
walkthrough_steps: Confirm inside/outside interface designation and reachability.
Create object network for inside subnet.
Apply dynamic PAT to outside interface.
Review/adjust access policy to permit test flow.
Generate test traffic from inside toward outside target.
Inspect xlate and connection tables for expected entries.
Run packet-tracer and reconcile any deny outputs.
coaching_notes: No translation appears without matching traffic; always generate traffic first.
Inside/outside reversal is a frequent configuration error.

rhel9_nmcli_static_ip_dns.title: RHEL9 Guided Build: nmcli Static IP and DNS Baseline
rhel9_nmcli_static_ip_dns.symptom: Configure a RHEL9 endpoint with static addressing and DNS using nmcli, then validate resolver behavior.
requirements: Identify active NetworkManager connection profile for the target NIC.
Configure static IPv4 address and prefix on the active profile.
Configure default gateway and DNS server list.
Disable automatic DNS overwrite where required by profile behavior.
Bring connection down/up and confirm settings persist.
Verify reachability to gateway and DNS resolution for test hostname.

faults.fault: Endpoint starts with DHCP/default profile unsuitable for static lab target.
faults.fix: Apply static nmcli profile settings and validate persistency.

hints: Use nmcli -p connection show to avoid editing the wrong profile.
Apply ipv4.method manual when moving from DHCP to static config.
Cycle the connection profile to ensure runtime state matches saved settings.
expected_results: Interface has configured static IP/prefix after reconnect.
Default route points to intended gateway.
DNS servers are present and name resolution works for test queries.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab: endpoint baseline uses non-static defaults.
answer_key.fix_summary: Set static IPv4/gateway/DNS via nmcli and reactivate the profile.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch A guided build lab.
progression_rank: RHEL9 Guided Build: nmcli Static IP and DNS Baseline
walkthrough_steps: List devices and identify active connection profile.
Set ipv4.method manual with static address/prefix.
Set gateway and DNS servers on the same profile.
Bring profile down and back up.
Validate interface and route table state.
Validate resolver configuration and DNS lookup behavior.
Capture outputs for grading evidence.
coaching_notes: Most nmcli failures are profile-name mismatches, not syntax errors.
If DNS appears unchanged, check whether another service is managing resolv.conf.

ccna_standard_extended_acl_placement.title: CCNA Guided Build: Standard vs Extended ACL Placement
ccna_standard_extended_acl_placement.symptom: Design and apply standard and extended ACLs at proper locations while preserving required traffic.
requirements: Create one standard ACL for management-plane control.
Create one extended ACL for user-to-server policy filtering.
Apply standard ACL near destination and extended ACL near source per requirement set.
Permit required business traffic and deny disallowed flows.
Add explicit logging on deny statements where requested.
Verify ACL hit counts and reachability outcomes.

faults.fault: Baseline has no policy controls; ACL plan must be built from requirements.
faults.fix: Create and place ACLs correctly on required interfaces/directions.

hints: Place extended ACLs close to source and standard ACLs closer to destination.
Validate direction (in/out) per interface before applying ACL.
Use hit counters to confirm traffic is matching intended statements.
expected_results: Allowed flows succeed and blocked flows fail per policy matrix.
ACL counters increment on expected permit/deny lines.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab with no prebuilt ACL policy.
answer_key.fix_summary: Implement standard/extended ACLs with correct placement and interface direction.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch B guided build lab.
progression_rank: CCNA Guided Build: Standard vs Extended ACL Placement
walkthrough_steps: Review required permit/deny matrix.
Create standard ACL entries for management constraints.
Create extended ACL entries for app/user traffic policy.
Apply ACLs to correct interfaces in proper direction.
Test allow/deny behavior with representative traffic.
Inspect ACL counters and adjust sequence/order if needed.
coaching_notes: Wrong interface direction is the most common ACL bug.
Always include required implicit/explicit permit paths to avoid overblocking.

ccna_fhrp_hsrp_gateway_redundancy.title: CCNA Guided Build: HSRP Gateway Redundancy Baseline
ccna_fhrp_hsrp_gateway_redundancy.symptom: Configure resilient first-hop gateway services with HSRP and verify active/standby behavior.
requirements: Configure HSRP for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 SVIs on distribution switches.
Set virtual IP gateway per VLAN.
Set primary/secondary priorities and preempt policy.
Track at least one uplink object to trigger failover behavior.
Verify active/standby roles from both distribution devices.
Validate host default gateway continuity during failover event.

faults.fault: HSRP not configured in baseline for required VLANs.
faults.fix: Build HSRP groups, priorities, and tracking policy.

hints: Set deterministic priorities so expected active role is clear.
Enable preempt to restore preferred active device after recovery.
Test failover by administratively impacting tracked uplink.
expected_results: HSRP groups elect expected active/standby devices.
Virtual IP remains reachable during failover.
Role transition behavior matches configured priority/tracking.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab: first-hop redundancy omitted from baseline.
answer_key.fix_summary: Configure HSRP groups with VIP, priority, preempt, and tracking on both peers.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch B guided build lab.
progression_rank: CCNA Guided Build: HSRP Gateway Redundancy Baseline
walkthrough_steps: Identify VLAN SVIs participating in gateway redundancy.
Configure HSRP group and virtual IP on DIST1 VLAN interfaces.
Configure matching HSRP groups on DIST2 with lower priority.
Enable preempt and add uplink tracking where required.
Verify active/standby state and priorities.
Trigger failover and confirm gateway continuity.
coaching_notes: HSRP group/VLAN mismatches cause silent failures.
Failover testing is mandatory; config alone is not proof.

ccnp_ospf_multi_area_abrs_filtering.title: CCNP Guided Build: OSPF Multi-Area ABR Filtering

Define ABR router IDs and stable adjacency policy.
Implement area range summarization at ABR where required.
Apply prefix filtering/distribution policy per scenario requirements.
Verify LSA visibility and routing table outcomes in each area.
Demonstrate policy effect before/after applying ABR controls.

faults.fault: ABR policy controls and summaries are absent in baseline.
faults.fix: Implement multi-area ABR controls per requirements and verify route propagation behavior.

hints: Stabilize adjacencies before applying summarization/filtering knobs.
Validate policy from downstream area perspective, not just ABR output.
Capture baseline route table before policy changes for comparison.
expected_results: Inter-area routes reflect configured summaries/policies.
Denied prefixes are absent where expected while required routes remain present.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab: ABR policy behavior is intentionally undeployed in starter state.
answer_key.fix_summary: Implement area design, ABR summaries, and filtering controls per requirements.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch B guided build lab.
progression_rank: CCNP Guided Build: OSPF Multi-Area ABR Filtering
walkthrough_steps: Confirm topology area boundaries and ABR roles.
Establish OSPF adjacencies for area 0 and non-backbone area.
Set ABR route summarization directives where required.
Apply area/filter policy for permitted/blocked prefixes.
Compare route tables and LSDB views before and after policy.
Remediate any unintended reachability loss.
coaching_notes: ABR filtering mistakes can blackhole large route sets; validate incrementally.
Use controlled baseline snapshots to prove policy effect.

ccnp_qos_classification_marking_policy.title: CCNP Guided Build: QoS Classification, Marking, and Policy Application

Create policy-map with DSCP marking and bandwidth/priority behavior per requirements.
Apply service-policy on intended interface/direction.
Generate representative traffic classes for validation.

Adjust policy ordering if class matches are not behaving as intended.

faults.fix: Implement classification, marking, and service-policy attachment.

hints: Start by validating ACL/class-map match logic before touching policy-map actions.
Attach policy in the correct direction; wrong direction yields zero counters.
Use class counters as primary truth for matching behavior.
expected_results: Traffic classes match expected counters.
DSCP/priority behavior aligns with policy requirements.

answer_key.root_cause: Build lab: QoS controls are intentionally absent in baseline.
answer_key.fix_summary: Create class-map/policy-map and apply service-policy in correct direction.

qa_notes: Wave 1 Batch B guided build lab.
progression_rank: CCNP Guided Build: QoS Classification, Marking, and Policy Application
walkthrough_steps: Define class-maps for required traffic classes.
Build policy-map actions including marking/priority directives.
Apply policy to target interface in required direction.
Generate traffic for each class.
Inspect class counters and policy results.
Refine match/action order until outcomes align with requirements.
coaching_notes: Zero packet counters usually mean wrong attachment point/direction or match criteria mismatch.

encor-core.title: ENCOR Core Practical Path
encor-core.description: A concise path through representative labs for the main non-controller ENCOR technologies.

steps.title: Campus Layer 2 fundamentals
steps.objective: Validate VLANs, trunks, STP, and EtherChannel troubleshooting.

steps.title: First-hop redundancy and access edge services
steps.objective: Troubleshoot HSRP behavior and common access-edge protection features.

steps.title: OSPF and IPv6/OSPFv3
steps.objective: Practice OSPFv2, IPv6, and OSPFv3 adjacency/path issues.

steps.title: Path control and external reachability
steps.objective: Cover BGP, PBR, NAT, and default-route style troubleshooting.

steps.title: Virtualization and tunneling
steps.objective: Practice VRF-Lite and GRE issues without requiring controllers.

steps.title: Security and access hardening
steps.objective: Troubleshoot ACLs, AAA, CoPP, ASAv, and edge-security failures.

steps.title: Network assurance
steps.objective: Validate monitoring and operational visibility components.

steps.title: QoS and multicast
steps.objective: Troubleshoot QoS policy behavior and multicast forwarding.

steps.title: Automation and architecture
steps.objective: Practice automation interpretation and design-level reasoning.

encor-complete.title: ENCOR Complete Domain Sweep
encor-complete.description: A longer sweep organized by ENCOR domain. Use this after the core path or for comprehensive review.

steps.title: Architecture
steps.objective: Review campus, overlay/underlay, gateway placement, and resiliency design decisions.

steps.title: Virtualization
steps.objective: Troubleshoot VRF and tunnel-based segmentation/transport labs.

steps.title: Infrastructure
steps.objective: Review the largest ENCOR domain: L2, routing, IPv6, QoS, multicast, NAT, and FHRP.

steps.title: Network Assurance
steps.objective: Verify syslog, SNMP, NetFlow, SPAN/RSPAN, IP SLA, and NTP visibility.

steps.title: Security
steps.objective: Review device access, ACLs, CoPP, firewall behavior, and access-edge security controls.

steps.title: Automation
steps.objective: Review JSON, REST/NETCONF/YANG, EEM, and Python parsing tasks.

steps.title: Advanced routing depth
steps.objective: Practice redistribution, filtering, summarization, default origination, and path-selection edge cases.

steps.title: Security policy depth
steps.objective: Practice ASAv NAT/ACL/object-policy edge cases plus IOS ACL, uRPF, and management-plane hardening.

steps.title: Automation and assurance workflow depth
steps.objective: Practice mock API parsing, telemetry interpretation, and automation workflow troubleshooting.

steps.title: Skill checks
steps.objective: Complete configure-from-requirements labs, ending with the enterprise WAN capstone.

steps.title: ENCOR skill-check expansion
steps.objective: Complete dedicated ENCOR configure-from-requirements skill checks before the enterprise WAN capstone.

skill-checks.title: Skill Checks by Exam
skill-checks.description: Configuration-from-requirements labs that increase in difficulty from CCNA access-edge skills to an ENCOR/ENARSI enterprise WAN capstone.

steps.title: CCNA access edge skill check
steps.objective: Configure a small access edge from requirements.

steps.title: ENCOR campus routing/services skill check
steps.objective: Configure campus routing, QoS, and access-edge behavior.

steps.title: ENARSI advanced routing skill check
steps.objective: Configure redistribution, filtering, summarization, default origination, and BGP policy.

steps.title: ENCOR enterprise WAN capstone
steps.objective: Configure HQ, multiple field offices, ISP transit, and partner reachability.

steps.title: ENCOR IPv6 and dual-stack checks
steps.objective: Validate IPv6 and dual-stack configuration skill.

steps.title: ENCOR routing checks
steps.objective: Validate OSPF, EIGRP, and BGP configuration skill.

steps.title: ENCOR policy/workflow checks
steps.objective: Validate QoS, security, automation, and assurance skill.

tagging_policy.description: Tags are normalized search/filter labels for GUI lab discovery. Exam tags remain separate and should not be used only to indicate conceptual overlap.
tagging_policy.ccna_prefix_rule: Scenarios beginning with ccna_ are CCNA-only and should not be included in ENCOR study paths.
tagging_policy.study_plan_order: Study plans should follow exam domain order first, then difficulty/progression, then topic/title.
